title: Adaptive probing and graceful de-escalation for tenant burst resilience
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: After the 2026-03-02 hosted API capacity exhaustion, we observed rapid tenant-driven queue amplification that overloaded GPU pools before autoscaler/reactive admission could stabilize. This ticket implements a multi-pronged mitigation: (1) lightweight adaptive probing to detect tenant burst patterns, (2) a graceful de-escalation path that throttles and deprioritizes bursty requests rather than hard-failing, (3) short-lived micro-quotas and tenant soft-landing to prevent cascade eviction, and (4) telemetry and runbook improvements to accelerate detection and remediation. Objective: prevent end-to-end GPU pool exhaustion and reduce customer-visible 5xxs during tenant spikes while preserving throughput for steady workloads.
acceptance_criteria: New burst-detection metric (tenant_burst_score) emitted with <1s latency and validated in staging
Adaptive probe flow implemented and gated by a feature flag; probes do not increase tail latency by >2% in load test
Soft-deprioritization path returns informative 429/202 style responses with retry hints and does not cause queue amplification
Micro-quota soft-landing reduces pool-level queue growth by >=40% in chaos test scenarios compared to baseline
Runbook updated with automated escalation steps and a one-click rollback for the probe feature flag
tasks: Design probe heuristic and score (owner: Diego) - implement tenant_burst_score using EWMA of arrival rate and KV cache eviction rate
Admission controller change (owner: Priya R.) - add soft-deprioritize code path + metrics and expose per-tenant micro-quotas
Runtime integration (owner: Marcus L.) - ensure probe decisions are available to scheduler without cross-pool RPCs
Load and chaos tests (owner: QA Team: Kent) - create attack profile and validate thresholds
Console and alerts (owner: Olivia) - add tenant_burst_score dashboard, set alert thresholds and playbook links
Documentation and runbook (owner: Aisha) - postmortem addendum, operator checklist, rollback steps
decisions: Use soft-deprioritization instead of immediate hard-eviction to preserve best-effort throughput for low-latency tenants
Probe approach: cheap client-side sampling + server-side EWMA to avoid stabilizer-induced feedback loops
Start with conservative default thresholds and iterate after simulated tenant spike tests; larger customers can opt into stricter policies via tenant config
Avoid cross-pool coordination on the fast path to minimize RPC surface and failure blast radius; accept some false positives in favor of low latency
KV-cache eviction rate included in score because prior incidents showed cache pollution correlated with tail latency spikes

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez: Prototype EWMA probe implemented in staging. Observed a small number of false positives with one synthetic workload that uses extreme short sequences. Planning to add KV-cache eviction smoothing.

2026-03-12 - Priya Rao: Reviewed prototype. Suggested switching to soft-429 semantics with Retry-After header and a structured reason payload for SDKs to surface. Also requested per-tenant opt-in controls for stricter enforcement.

2026-03-13 - Marcus Liu: Integrated probe decision into scheduler path using shared in-process cache for low-latency access. Noted a race with autoscaler signals; added a short-lived lease token to prevent immediate eviction loops.

Initial run shows 37% reduction in pool-level queue growth when soft-deprioritization is enabled; tail latency impact negligible for steady clients. One test revealed flaky cleanup in the runtime that can leak probe tokens - blocking fix added to PR.
